findings.F1: The tested idea, that deeper scaled dips fall more over 5 days, is on its own side but far from the bar: the main measure's mean is 0.0052 with t 0.61 (715 cases, 239 days), and its size is an unusual move of +0.04 % per case with t 0.09 (1159 cases, 594 days), 0.000 of the usual 11.68 % move.
findings.F2: At the plan's 5-day horizon inside rising calm (folds B and C, 265 cases on 101 days), the depth is not graded: the product has t 0.09, and the mean excess 5-day return is -1.21 % for the deepest third, +1.30 % for the middle third and +0.81 % for the shallowest third, so the supporting check passed only because of the deepest third.
findings.F3: Over shorter horizons inside rising calm, the depth points toward recovery, the brief's own effect: with the depth recomputed from prices, deeper dips are followed by a higher excess return over 1 day (product t +2.13, Spearman -0.108, mean excess +0.45 %, 1011 cases on 413 days) and over 3 days (t +1.98, Spearman -0.264, mean excess +0.70 %, 323 cases on 139 days); the plan's forecast-based product agrees, with t -1.73 over 1 day and -1.88 over 3 days (negative here means recovery).
findings.F4: The short-horizon recovery is specific to rising calm: in other markets the same depth measure shows nothing, with 1-day t of -0.82 (choppy), -0.16 (falling) and +0.04 (rising agitated), and 3-day t of -0.80, -1.07 and +0.34.
findings.F5: The 5-day effect is mixed across periods and coins: the product is -0.041 in 2020 (106 cases), +0.017 in 2021 (90 cases) and +0.118 in 2018 (18 cases), and it is positive on 5 of the 10 coins and negative on the other 5.
findings.F6: No more data is available than the test used, since it already ran all 19 coins on all four folds; the short book also lost (Sharpe -0.77), because its total move per case of -0.69 % comes from the coin's normal drift against a short (-0.73 %) and costs 3.1 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, the further a coin's close sits below its highest close of the past 5 days, measured against its usual daily swing over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader can buy a deep scaled pullback in a calm uptrend for a 3-day bounce, sized larger the deeper the dip, instead of shorting it or holding it for 5 days.
ideas.name: calm uptrend dips bounce briefly
